content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increase — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price spikes.
- After sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 79.80, 80.24), model forecasts overshoot or fail to peak accurately, then overcorrect.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — overestimates decline after peaks, underestimates recovery after troughs.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days are often too high, suggesting overconfidence in short-term momentum or failure to account for volatility decay.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of the price distribution — underestimates extreme lows and overestimates extreme highs in the final days.
- Forecasts are systematically too conservative in the first 10 days, then become more aggressive — possibly due to misaligned horizon weighting or lagged signal processing.
